title: Destiny 2’s Returning Content Makes This The Perfect Time To Grab Its Complete DLC Bundle
description: I have a love-hate relationship with Destiny 2. I love the game and hate the fact that most of the content from Forsaken and before has essentially vanished, making it harder to recommend to newcomers. With active development set to end after the release of Renegades in The Fate Saga, the fact that much of The Light and Darkness Saga was unplayable was a sad fate. Now, Bungie is bringing back older content, sweeping open the door to the vault, and that means getting the entire Destiny 2 experience at a low price is worth picking up. Destiny 2 is at its best when you can play through the entire narrative, from The Red War onward. Of course, Destiny 1 being limited to older-generation consoles isn't brilliant, but the fact that most of the saga is in the sequel makes it mostly fine. Yet Bungie's vaulting of previously playable Destiny 2 content was never a great move. Since the announcement that the game was no longer receiving content, I had stopped playing. Now, this gives me and many other Guardians a chance to play again, and for newcomers, it means not missing out on valuable lore. It would take me a long time to explain the lore, but basically, a white ball in the sky resurrects warriors to fight against darkness; you are one of those warriors. You choose which class you want to play as, between Hunter, Warlock, or Titan—each with its own strengths—and battle enemies across the solar system. Oh, and you need to farm for loot, including the coveted Exotic gear, which consists of game-changing pieces of equipment that can help you build a powerful Guardian. It's one of the best FPS games out there. Bungie's gunplay remains solid and consistent a decade after release, and Destiny 2 is still one of my favorite looters to play. Shredding hordes of Vex is as satisfying as it has ever been. The DLCs are easily some of the best in the genre, with The Witch Queen and The Final Shape being some of the greatest expansions in gaming—our Final Shape review is proof of that.…

title: Should you participate in GTA 6's Safe Word mission?
GTA 6’s Furry Rescue Mission Is A Little Weird, But The Rewards Are Worth It
description: No matter what you do in GTA 6, it pales in comparison to being a Furry in that game. Anyone looking to externalize their inner animal spirit is in danger of being hunted, and you'll find out for yourself just how much the fictional state of Leonida hates Furries when you're given the chance to save one of them from being murdered by the cops. Should you help them? Absolutely, if you want an easy payday or a new weapon for your arsenal. How to find Chase the Fox Like several other missions in GTA 6, helping out the Furry resistance appears to trigger randomly. The mission takes place after Chapter 3, on Miramar Drive in Crosstown, Vice City, and you'll want to be cruising around that area at night, between midnight and 4 AM. Once it starts, you'll see cops pull up to hunt down a Furry by the name of Chase, and if you drive up to him, you can either give him a lift or leave him to his brutal fate. Outrun the cops If you do choose to help Chase, then get ready to be hunted down by cops. You'll pick up a three-star Wanted level, which means the cops will be in mildly hot pursuit of your vehicle. Reach the parking garage Chase will direct you to a nearby parking garage, where his Furry allies are waiting. After a short standoff, they'll welcome you into their ranks as an honorary Furry. Courier the group to safety To get the law off your polyester tail, one of your new allies will take your car and use it to distract the cops. Get inside the van, and you can bring the other Furries home to their swanky pad in Starfish Island. While you're driving, the Furries will interact with each other, and you can watch their hijinks. Choose your reward Once Chase and his pals are back home, you'll be offered one of two rewards: $15,000 in cash or the unique Furry DW-9 submachine gun. Personally, I'd go with the gun since it's easy enough to make cash in GTA 6, and having more weapons is never a bad idea. You'll also gain safehouse access to the Furry group's hideout, where you can…

title: You Can Find Lucia’s Discarded Gun From The GTA 6 Prologue
description: In the prologue sequence for GTA 6, Lucia finds herself in a bit of trouble, forced to discard a handgun she'd used to hold up a store. However, it's not lost forever. You can return to the store and find the gun nearby, but this is easier to do in Chapter 3, once you've made it to Vice City. To find the gun, you'll want to head to the Little Cuba area of Vice City, just off the large highway. There's an area with Rosita's Cuban Cafe and the payday loans shop that Lucia holds up. The gun isn't found on the street; you'll have to take to the rooftops and search for it. The pink marker shows where Lucia's gun can be picked up. Climb to the roof of the payday loans store and head toward the canal. Look for the air conditioning units and a round metal vent. You'll find the beaten up Low Point Nipper.38 on top of the vent itself. We were playing as Lucia when we picked it up, but it unlocks for her and Jason once you've collected it. Lucia's gun is on top of the vent nearby. For more on the weird goings-on around Leonida, from alien sightings to a free tank, check out our GTA 6 guides hub.

title: Mario, Pikachu, And Other Gaming Icon Balloons Won’t Be Flying This Thanksgiving
description: New York City is no stranger to bad weather, be it blazing-hot summers, snow-packed winters, or fierce windstorms. Unfortunately for countless families who have made it a holiday tradition to turn on the TV and watch giant totems of pop culture sail in the streets of the great city, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been officially delayed due to a forecast of rain and windstorms--a first in its 100-year history. In recent years, gaming icons have become more and more prominent during the parade. Beginning in 1993, a balloon of Sonic the Hedgehog marked the first game character to float among the procession. Since then, more characters have joined the festivities, including Mario, Pac-Man, Pikachu, and even Red the Angry Bird, among others. However, those who have followed the history of Macy's balloons know that the mix of bad weather and massive, floating objects can result in genuine danger for balloon handlers, bystanders, and objects on the streets. Rather infamously, Sonic's 1993 appearance was marred by an incident where the balloon got stuck on a lamppost, popping the balloon and injuring two bystanders. Other balloon bursts have proved even more catastrophic, with a series of mishaps in 1997 leading to a Cat in the Hat balloon causing injuries that left a woman comatose for days. Since then, more emphasis has rightfully been put on safety. While it might be disappointing to not be able to point at the TV and go "Mario!" with your younger cousins around the TV tomorrow, the balloons will get a chance to fly on Saturday starting at 8:30 AM ET, when the weather is likely to be significantly less awful. You can find other ways to fill the time--but maybe ask your relatives first if it's okay to let the kiddos watch you play GTA 6. Image credit: Getty Images / Craig T Fruchtman

title: How To Talk To Your Relatives (And Their Cool-Ass Kids) About GTA 6 This Thanksgiving
description: Every Thanksgiving brings the possibility of fraught conversations. Your sister's divorce. Your second cousin's polycule. Politics. So surely one of the biggest entertainment launches of all time, and certainly the biggest one of the year, will come up in conversation. Your relatives might not know much about Grand Theft Auto 6, and as the designated video gamer of the family, all eyes may turn to you to explain what's going on. How do you broach this delicate topic with your loved ones? How do you explain what's so special and momentous about this moment in video games? Do you show them Mandy? (Don't.) In the interest of doing our due diligence and public service, we've compiled a brief guide on how to talk with your family about GTA 6 this Thanksgiving. Somewhere in between the parade and your third slice of pie, your relatives may come away with a better understanding of this cultural moment, and of video games more broadly. Grand Theft Auto 6 What's the big deal, anyway? Grand Theft Auto 6 made nearly $4 billion on its first day of release, and sold an astonishing 32.5 million copies. That's a number that most entertainment properties would love to hit in lifetime sales, and GTA did it in a day. That also puts it on-track to be one of the biggest entertainment launches of all time, rivaling most big-budget movies in lifetime grosses. Analysts have compared it to everything from The Avengers to Taylor Swift. Aside from the financial success, it's also a critical hit. At a 99 Metacritic rating, it has tied for the top-reviewed game of all time. The other contender is the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which got a well-regarded but not as high-scoring remake this year. So GTA 6 is about as close as we're getting to a monoculture in today's fractious media environment. Everybody online is talking about it and responding to it and the discourse is shaping a lot of conversation. So even if you aren't actively playing it, chances are you're…

title: How To Rob Banks In GTA 6
description: It goes without saying that you’ll commit countless crimes in Grand Theft Auto 6. From punching hapless civilians and stealing their cars, to threatening storeowners as you take their hard-earned cash, the world is yours for the taking. Now, you’re about to level up as you rob banks all over Leonida. These require you to play through the campaign until you reach chapter 3, whereupon you’ll be able to tackle various main missions for two NPCs: Raul and Yasmani. Dye Pack Jammer You receive this permanent upgrade as part of a main mission called Credit Check. Prior to this point, any packets of marked money you obtain may have anti-theft devices that explode. Whenever this occurs, your character will be covered in a bright pink color, making it easier for cops to recognize you. Worse, the marked money will be defaced and ruined, rendering it useless. Snap Gun During chapter 3, you’ll be introduced to Yasmani, who’ll task you with hitting three jewelry stores in Vice City. Do these objectives to receive the Snap Gun, a tool that enables a lockpicking minigame. This lets you open locked doors, which could be used as alternate entrances. So, anytime you’ve got marked money on you, be sure to exchange it with him. Note: Yasmani also gives you info on which banks might have a lot more cash than usual, but this info comes at a price. title: How To Open Bank Vaults In GTA 6
description: From the start of Chapter 4 in Grand Theft Auto 6, you'll get the opportunity to rob banks in GTA 6. Previously, you could rob pawn shops, jewelry stores, and other small-time locations. However, after receiving the Dye Pack Jammer from Karim, you can rob big-time banks by stealing all of its marked bills. Robbing a big bank has its challenges, though, and one of the tougher problems they present is breaking into the vault. Every big bank has a vault you can rob in GTA 6, but they can't be opened using traditional methods. If you want the biggest score possible, though, you'll have to learn the one method to break into any bank vault. How to get inside any bank vault in GTA 6 Chances are, if you're reading this guide, you tried to rob a large Fleeca bank only to make it inside and realize the vault door is closed. Unlike the bank's safe, you can't enter a code or use one of your lockpicking tools to open the vault and steal all the cash inside. While there are rare instances where you might find a bank's vault open, they're almost always closed unless you use one specific method in GTA 6. The only way to break into a bank vault is by waiting for an armored security truck driver to open it themselves. You might have seen these trucks driving around the map, but their sole job is to deliver briefcases full of cash inside bank vaults across Vice City. You can get lucky and spot one of these trucks yourself, but the best way to locate them is by going through Yasmani. Yasmani is a fence whom you meet during Chapter 3 through Boobie. At first, Yasmani just looks like another fence who buys illegal goods from you in GTA 6. However, as you progress, it's revealed that Yasmani can offer you tips on potential jobs in exchange for a small fee. Yasmani is a fence in GTA 6, but also offers tips on money-making jobs. The one job you're looking for from Yasmani is a tip about a security truck that is planned to make a stop at a bank vault. This tip costs you $10,000 every time,…

title: All Missable Missions In GTA 6 And How To Start Them
description: Strangers and Freaks have returned in GTA 6. Though you only see these missable side missions referred to in that way in the Achievement and Trophy lists, there are still some weird NPCs who offer wild missions across Leonida. Instead of being called "Strangers and Freaks" missions, you'll just see a character's initials in an icon on your map. As a general tip, their mission markers are black icons with pink lettering, the inverse of a main-story mission's color coding--pink icons with black lettering. These aren't missable missions in the sense that you lose them directly because of how time passes in GTA 6 day to day, which the game flags with an hourglass icon on the mission marker. There are also missions, such as Kenton's treasure dives in chapter 1, that can become locked for a period of time as you progress through the story, but these will unlock later. Instead, you need to find these "Stranger and Freak" NPCs in GTA 6 within their relevant chapters, or else--at least in some cases--you'll miss the chance to kick off their questlines. Thankfully, most of them begin with texts or calls you won't miss if you're diligently glued to your phone like a modern American is expected to be. Below, you can see all Strangers and Freaks missions in GTA 6 and where the NPCs who offer them are located. We're only counting NPCs that you don't meet through the main story or those who have an entirely separate questline from the story. title: What Is The Point Of No Return In The GTA 6 Story?
description: We've never seen a main story in the Grand Theft Auto franchise like the one in GTA 6. It's an absolute behemoth, stretching across five chapters and just under 100 main story missions. It'll take you at least around 45-50 hours to get through the story if you're solely focusing on it. However, if you're also partaking in some side content, then you'll want to know when the "point of no return" is during the GTA 6 story. This is essentially when the game locks you out of anything aside from reaching the end credits and finishing the story. So, if you want to finish up any loose ends in Leonida, you need to know when the point of no return occurs. Warning: there are spoilers for the GTA 6 main story below. What leads up to the point of no return in GTA 6? Fortunately, Rockstar Games makes it fairly clear as to when the point of no return is in GTA 6. However, the decision to continue on with the story until the end is somewhat thrust upon you, so it's still worth knowing what leads up to this moment. During Chapter 5, Jason and Lucia have two primary goals: get out of Vice City and make enough money so they can support Tommy in a new life. To accomplish both of those goals, the protagonists work with Valentina, their money launderer and political go-between, to secure a deal for their coveted hard drive. The deal could be worth a lot of money, but Jason and Lucia also need to shore up their immediate finances so they have something to live off once they escape Leonida and start over with Tommy. In the background of all this, the pair's lawyer, Abe, is working with the U.S. government to secure a pardon for them, which expunges their record of all illegal acts they've committed. To push the pardon through, though, you need to fork over a whopping $150,000 to Abe's law firm as a service fee. When does the point of no return happen in GTA 6? After you BuckMe that tidy sum to the law firm, you'll receive a new story mission on the map marked with Abe's initials. If you…
